Looking at the [results](https://bench.meilisearch.dev/view_spans?commit_sha1=c41929db3ef5f03896a56b46b245077fd959d15c&workload_name=settings-add-remove-filters.json&target_branch=avoid-clearing-db-in-transform), it seems all benchmarks lost 3s total time, or 10% on average.

Looking in details, the differences are in the `extract_*` and `sorter_into_reader`, but the number of calls are identical, so I'd say this is probably noise?

What was the *expected* effect of this PR on spans?
Should we maybe have more spans in the transform part of the indexing?

@dureuill,
this shouldn't change anything because I didn't modify the indexer when running the benchmarks. Should we raise the number of iterations in each workload?

I don't know, could be due to the worker it has run on, too.

Looking at the spans in details, I think it is relatively clear that it is noise.
Ok, I ran this in order to have a reference when comparing the indexer versions

Some results:

- [`settings-add-remove-filters.json`](https://bench.meilisearch.dev/view_spans?commit_sha1=9b20024e3a29e0fe61596552ff364ae60d646533&workload_name=settings-add-remove-filters.json&target_branch=avoid-clearing-db-in-transform&baseline_branch=main): -8s (from 33 to 26). Mostly we seem to be writing less, and we have a huge win on [`indexing::extract::words_into_sorter](https://bench.meilisearch.dev/view_span?span=indexing::extract::words_into_sorter&workload_name=settings-add-remove-filters.json&target=9b20024e3a29e0fe61596552ff364ae60d646533&baseline=75f81a0babe8b0d70364e91a22db22fb94bc8e44&baseline_branch=main&target_branch=avoid-clearing-db-in-transform) with the call count going from 2_699_991 to 899_997. We're also using [grenad_sorter_into_reader](https://bench.meilisearch.dev/view_span?span=indexing::grenad::sorter_into_reader&workload_name=settings-add-remove-filters.json&target=9b20024e3a29e0fe61596552ff364ae60d646533&baseline=75f81a0babe8b0d70364e91a22db22fb94bc8e44&baseline_branch=main&target_branch=avoid-clearing-db-in-transform) less.
- Non-significant win for `settings-proximity-precision.json`. Looks like the wins on facets::bulk::execute are counter-balanced by losses on [`extract_docid_word_positions`](https://bench.meilisearch.dev/view_span?span=indexing::extract::extract_docid_word_positions&workload_name=settings-proximity-precision.json&target=9b20024e3a29e0fe61596552ff364ae60d646533&baseline=75f81a0babe8b0d70364e91a22db22fb94bc8e44&baseline_branch=main&target_branch=avoid-clearing-db-in-transform)
- Significant losses for the other two workloads: -5s and -2s. looking into the why, there is [`flatten_from_fields_ids_map`](https://bench.meilisearch.dev/view_span?span=indexing::transform::flatten_from_fields_ids_map&workload_name=settings-remove-add-swap-searchable.json&target=9b20024e3a29e0fe61596552ff364ae60d646533&baseline=75f81a0babe8b0d70364e91a22db22fb94bc8e44&baseline_branch=main&target_branch=avoid-clearing-db-in-transform) that gets called much more, and otherwise it looks like we're doing more indexing work

issue_context.title: Avoid a full index deletion in `Transform` when changing settings
issue_context.body:
Related product team resources: [PRD](https://www.notion.so/meilisearch/Settings-diff-indexing-work-5d77d81761934a5aab32bebd163197af?pvs=4) (_internal only_)

## Summary

This issue is a subset of the work implementing the settings diff-indexing enhancement.

The current approach of [`Transform::prepare_for_documents_reindexing`](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/blob/main/milli/src/update/index_documents/transform.rs#L811-L954) is to dump all the documents in the index into a `Grenad::File` and delete the whole index to reindex all the documents, taking into account the `Settings` changes.

This function should instead create document deltas without clearing the index.

## TODO

- [x] Ensure Meilisearch has tests triggering the [`Transform::prepare_for_documents_reindexing`](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/blob/main/milli/src/update/index_documents/transform.rs#L811-L954) methods
- [x] Make both [`into_del_add_obkv` calls](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/blob/main/milli/src/update/index_documents/transform.rs#L811-L954) use `DelAddOperation::DeletionAndAddition`
- [x] Remove [`ClearDocuments` calls
](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/blob/d44e20aa8952e7bfb04fdcfcbfc5cce94f93d1f7/milli/src/update/index_documents/transform.rs#L950)

review_comments: The implementation was wrong, the user_defined_faceted_fields_ids was getting all the faceted fields

We now have different versions of the settings for the old and the new values.
Because the old version was computed with the old settings, we have to use them instead of the new one to remove the old data from the database

We now check both settings versions to know if we must remove a facet or add a new one.

We may use a xor here 🤔
The vector field id may have changed because of the field_ids_maps changes, so we have to get each vector field separately even if they are in the same field id 99% of the time.
Vector indexing is triggered if there is any embedding settings change of if there is any new document
if deletion contains ProximityPrecision::ByAttribute -> no deletion needed
if addition contains ProximityPrecision::ByAttribute -> no addition needed
The `fields_ids_map` is now provided because there are two maps, one for the old settings and one for the new ones.
Added `dimensions` because the indexer makes an API call to estimate dimensions even if there is no document in the DB
The settings diff needs the user_defined_searchable_fields_ids
we now force the reindexing if the searchable settings changed
The settings diff struct is now in charge of triggering or not a reindexing
it should be removed in the future in favor of a more granular embeddings indexing process
